title: continuity-gate: phased opt-in flags and regression suite for streaming, tool-calls, and structured outputs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: introduce an explicit compatibility gating mechanism (continuity-gate) that lets us retire legacy inference behaviors behind opt-in flags, provide automated migration guidance for customers using streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs, and validate regressions via a CI-driven backward-compatibility test suite. This ticket scopes the engineering deliverables: feature flag design, server-side enforcement, SDK flag propagation, a migration checklist, and an automated regression harness that runs against a curated corpus of prompts and tool-calls.
acceptance_criteria: continuity-gate flags implemented on the router and runtime layers: streaming_legacy_mode, toolcall_compat_v1, structured_output_loose_parsing
SDKs (JS + Python) propagate opt-in flags and documentation links in client warnings
Migration guide published and linked in console release notes
CI job ci/compat/regression-suite runs nightly and fails the release pipeline on high-severity regressions
Canary rollout path exists to enable/disable flags per-customer in Console and via API
migration_steps: 1) Create migration doc: outline common failure modes for streaming and tool-calls, with example inputs and expected outputs
2) Publish SDK helper that toggles flags and provides a compatibility shim for immediate opt-in
3) Provide a diagnostic endpoint /compat/check that runs customer prompts against both modes and returns diff summary
4) Offer a migration window: default to legacy behavior for 90 days after flag introduction, then auto-hover to opt-in for new accounts
5) Notify customers: email + Console banner with links to migration doc and test harness
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal): feature flags enabled for Redwood-internal orgs only, collect telemetry (2 weeks)
Phase B (beta): opt-in enabled for selected customers via Console toggle + support-managed opt-ins (4 weeks)
Phase C (broad): enable opt-in flags as default for new accounts; legacy mode still available as explicit flag for 90 days
Phase D (retire): after migration window and no critical regressions, deprecate legacy flags and schedule removal in a future release
test_plan: Create compat corpus (500 prompts) covering: short/long context streaming, partially-specified tool-calls, nested structured output examples, and edge-case tokenization sequences
Implement CI job ci/compat/regression-suite that: runs inference against both legacy and new modes, computes semantic and structural diffs, and classifies regressions into severity buckets
Add unit tests for flag evaluation logic in router and runtime (coverage > 90% for gate code paths)
E2E smoke tests: SDK toggles + server-side checks, include flow that exercises /compat/check and returns human-readable diffs
Create a nightly anomaly detection job that alerts on unexpected increases in regression-rate (>1% high-severity)
